headline: Brent crude extends losses on hopes for de-escalation in US-Iran conflict
summary: Brent crude oil prices fell 0.6% to $94.04 per barrel, following an 8.7% decline in the previous session. The slide is attributed to market optimism regarding a potential end to the conflict between the U.S. and Iran.
why: Oil prices are a critical driver of global inflation and industrial costs. Geopolitical tensions in the Middle East are a primary risk factor for energy supply chains.
why_moved: Markets price in a risk premium for potential supply disruptions during conflicts; the prospect of peace removes this premium, leading to lower prices.
